visa_policy.notes: Bolivia uses a 3-tier country grouping: Group I (no visa required for tourism), Group II (standard tourism visa required, 20 calendar days advance), Group III (visa with prior DIGEMIG consultation, 50-60 calendar days advance). Maximum stay for ALL tourists (including Group I) is 90 days per calendar year per Decreto Supremo 1923 Art. 9; the embassy EU page notes an initial 30-day stamp extendable twice. In December 2025, Bolivia's Foreign Ministry officially eliminated politically-motivated visa restrictions for 8 countries: USA, South Korea, South Africa, Bulgaria, Malta, Romania, UAE, and Israel (cancilleria.gob.bo/mre/2025/12/01/23577). The embajadadebolivia.eu page (crawled June 2026) has NOT been updated to reflect these December 2025 changes - it still lists South Korea in Group II and Israel in Group III; the cancilleria.gob.bo MFA announcement is the higher-authority and more recent source and takes precedence. Additional bilateral ordinary-passport visa-free agreements confirmed on cancilleria.gob.bo: Honduras (effective 17 March 2024), El Salvador (effective 21 June 2024), Dominican Republic (effective 2 September 2024). Russia: prior record included Russia in visa_free based on a 2016 bilateral agreement (cancilleria.gob.bo/mre/2016/04/12/8459); however, the embajadadebolivia.eu page (crawled June 2026) still lists Russia in Group II. Given the conflict between sources and the safety rule, Russia has been removed from visa_free and placed in data_quality.gaps pending re-verification against a current post-2022 official Bolivian source. MERCOSUR member nationals (Argentina, Brazil, Paraguay, Uruguay, Venezuela) and Mexico: no visa required for tourism; max stay 90 days per year per DS 1923. Andean Community members (Colombia, Ecuador, Peru) and Chile: 90-day visa-free entry. Visa-on-arrival for Group II nationals ended July 25, 2025 - Group II applicants must now obtain visas in advance. The official online visa application system is at visas.cancilleria.gob.bo. No e-visa or ETA system found on official sources. Chile-Bolivia agreement (March 2026) covers diplomatic/official passports only, does not affect ordinary-passport visa-free status already present in Group I.

conditional_access.conditions: Holders of diplomatic, official, or service passports of any country may enter Bolivia without a visa. Specific bilateral agreements confirmed: Equatorial Guinea (signed 23 November 2017, cancilleria.gob.bo/mre/2017/11/23/8345), Switzerland (signed 7 December 2018, cancilleria.gob.bo/mre/2018/12/07/7883; stay duration linked to period of functions/assignment), Honduras (March 2024, covering diplomatic and official passports), Chile (effective March 9, 2026, cancilleria.gob.bo/mre/2026/03/09/24588/, covers diplomatic and official passports for official travel). The blanket 90-day rule for all diplomatic/official/service passports is widely reported by Timatic but has not been confirmed verbatim on a directly-accessed official Bolivian government page beyond these specific bilateral agreements.

visa_types.name: Visa de Turismo o Visita
visa_types.purpose: Tourism, rest, recreation or visiting for nationals of Group II and Group III countries that require a visa (Group I nationals are visa-exempt).
visa_types.notes: Fee US$30 for most nationalities (Resolucion Ministerial 081/2015 consular tariff). A US$160 sticker fee historically applied to US/Puerto Rico passports, now moot since the US moved to visa-free Group I on 1 Dec 2025. Maximum stay is 90 days per calendar year (DS 1923 Art. 9); initial 30-day stamp extendable twice. Visa-on-arrival for Group II nationals ended 25 July 2025 - the visa must be obtained in advance at a consulate. Group II apply ~20 calendar days ahead; Group III ~50-60 days with prior DIGEMIG consultation.

visa_types.name: Visa de Objeto Determinado (Trabajo)
visa_types.purpose: Foreign nationals entering to work/be employed in Bolivia; entry visa that must be converted to temporary residence (permanencia temporal) at DIGEMIG.
visa_types.notes: Fee US$85 (arancel consular). Validity varies by purpose. Requires an invitation/employment letter from the Bolivian entity or company, a criminal-record certificate and proof of economic solvency. The holder has 30 days after entry to apply for temporary residence (permanencia temporal) before DIGEMIG.

visa_types.name: Visa de Objeto Determinado (Trabajo Temporal)
visa_types.purpose: Foreign nationals entering for temporary or seasonal work in Bolivia.
visa_types.notes: Fee US$85 (arancel consular); free of charge when issued under an inter-state agreement/convenio (trabajo temporal con convenio estatal). Distinct consular line item from the standard Objeto Determinado work visa.

visa_types.name: Visa de Estudiante
visa_types.purpose: Foreign nationals enrolling in primary, secondary, institute or university studies (including academic exchanges) in Bolivia.
visa_types.notes: Fee US$50 for regular students and exchange without a state agreement; free under a state exchange agreement (arancel consular). Valid up to 60 days, which enables the student to apply for a 1-year temporary residence (permanencia temporal) at DIGEMIG, renewable until studies are completed.

visa_types.name: Visa de Objeto Determinado (Salud)
visa_types.purpose: Foreign nationals entering Bolivia to receive medical treatment / for health reasons.
visa_types.notes: Fee US$85 (arancel consular; 'objeto determinado - salud'). Health is an explicitly listed purpose of the Visa de Objeto Determinado. Unlike work/multiple visas, no invitation letter or proof of economic solvency is required for the health sub-purpose.

visa_types.name: Visa de Objeto Determinado (Motivos Familiares)
visa_types.purpose: Foreign nationals entering to join or reunite with family members resident in Bolivia.
visa_types.notes: Fee US$85 (arancel consular; 'objeto determinado - familia'). Family is an explicitly listed purpose of the Visa de Objeto Determinado; no invitation letter or proof of economic solvency is required for the family sub-purpose. Typically converted to a family-based temporary residence at DIGEMIG.

visa_types.name: Visa Multiple
visa_types.purpose: Foreign investors and representatives of foreign companies carrying out investment and business activities in Bolivia; authorises repeated entry and exit.
visa_types.notes: Fee US$200 (arancel consular). Valid 1 year with multiple entries; each stay must not exceed 90 consecutive days. Requires legalised company incorporation documents, the company's tax ID (NIT) if constituted in Bolivia, and an INTERPOL criminal-record certificate. This is Bolivia's investor/business entry visa.

visa_types.name: Visa de Transito
visa_types.purpose: Foreign nationals transiting through Bolivian territory to a third-country final destination, including vessel and aircraft crew.
visa_types.notes: Free of charge (arancel consular). Maximum stay up to 15 days. Requires onward tickets proving the final destination is a third country.

visa_types.name: Visa Humanitaria
visa_types.purpose: For persons requiring international protection under the non-refoulement principle, victims of human trafficking or migrant smuggling, and companions of persons requiring medical treatment in Bolivia.
visa_types.notes: Free of charge per the consular arancel (consulados.cancilleria.gob.bo/base/arancel-consular/). Grants up to 30 days in Bolivian territory. Three eligible categories: (1) persons requiring international protection, (2) victims of human trafficking/migrant smuggling, (3) companions of persons requiring medical treatment. Requirements vary by category: sworn declaration form, passport valid 6+ months, yellow fever certificate (if applicable) and photo for standard applicants; proof of victim status for trafficking victims; medical certificate of necessity for medical companions. Exact entry count and processing time not specified on official source; 'single' assumed as the conservative default.

visa_types.name: Visa de Cortesía (Courtesy Visa)
visa_types.purpose: Issued to high-ranking state officials, government officials, international organization representatives, and cultural or religious personalities traveling on official or institutional business who do not otherwise qualify for a full diplomatic visa.
visa_types.notes: Free of charge per the consular arancel (consulados.cancilleria.gob.bo/base/arancel-consular/). Requires an invitation issued by a Bolivian public institution, channeled through the Ministry of Foreign Affairs. Max stay, validity, and entry count not specified on official source; 'single' assumed as the conservative default. Distinct from the passport-type-based diplomatic/official/service visa-free policy already recorded under conditional_access - this visa is for individuals invited in a courtesy capacity regardless of passport type.

cbi.notes: Bolivia has no official citizenship-by-investment (CBI) program. Bolivia's 2009 Constitution permits dual citizenship. Citizenship may be obtained after 3 years of continuous legal residency (standard naturalization path, not an investment program). No dedicated CBI program was found on any official Bolivian government source (migracion.gob.bo, cancilleria.gob.bo).

programs.name: Temporary Residency - Determined Purpose (Visa de Objeto Determinado) for Investors/Business
programs.notes: Foreign nationals who invest in Bolivian businesses, establish companies, or conduct business activities may apply for a 'Visa de Objeto Determinado' (Multiple Visa for investors/business). This visa is valid for 1 year with multiple entries; maximum 90-day stays per visit. After 2 years of temporary residency, MERCOSUR nationals can apply for permanent residency. After 3 years of continuous legal residency, any foreign national may apply for Bolivian citizenship. No minimum investment threshold is specified on official sources.

programs.name: Permanent Residency for MERCOSUR Nationals
programs.notes: Nationals of MERCOSUR member and associated states may apply for permanent residency after 2 years of valid temporary residence in Bolivia. Eligibility is governed by the MERCOSUR Residence Agreement. Bolivia formalized full MERCOSUR membership via Law 1567 (July 2024).

outbound_official.note: No official Bolivia government outbound visa-list page located. Bolivia's Cancillería (cancilleria.gob.bo) publishes individual press releases for each new bilateral visa-suppression agreement but maintains no single authoritative page listing all countries where Bolivian ordinary-passport holders can travel without a prior consular visa. The visa-application portal visas.cancilleria.gob.bo and the servicios/visas pages all address inbound (foreigners entering Bolivia) requirements only.
